takeaway: IMN Tuesday keeps Pacífico Norte in a typical ITCZ rainy-season day: isolated morning rains, possible isolated afternoon rain, and possible coastal rains tonight (Nicoya ~33°C). Hurricane Polo and TS Odalys stay well offshore Mexico/west EPAC — no cyclone near Costa Rica. Midweek SW Pacific moisture and flanking EPAC lows still show on ensemble means, but GEFS flips Nicoya back toward trades by ~Sun and NHC marine softens the CR–Guatemala low language, so the gyre/temporales watch stays elevated, not established.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Tue–Thu)
periods.pattern: Today (IMN Pacífico Norte, valid Tue 22 Sep): morning partial–mostly cloudy with isolated rains; afternoon partly cloudy with possible isolated rain; evening partial–mostly cloudy with possible coastal rains. General commentary: unstable ITCZ — dawn/early coastal Pacific rains that can push inland, afternoon Pacific-side storms (more emphasis inland/Valle Central and Caribbean mountains than a Pac Norte bullseye), night coastal Pacific rains again. Nicoya max ~32.7°C / min ~23.6°C (Liberia ~34°C). Weekly text: maritime Pacific rains more evident Mon–Wed mornings; OT#46 estimated this weekend with little country signal. GFS 06Z / GEFS mean 06Z / EPS mean 00Z 24-h maps keep Nicoya mostly light–moderate (~0.1–0.75 in / 24 h) through ~Wed morning. GEFS mean f024 shows light W–SW 850 flow with a ~999 hPa L off southern Mexico/Guatemala — moist monsoon trough / ITCZ, not a closed land gyre. Papagayo light SW ~10 kt, seas ~3–5 ft (NHC).
periods.implications: Mornings still the better outdoor window; plan around isolated afternoon–evening Pacific convection and possible overnight coastal rains. Inland Guanacaste stays hot (Liberia mid-30s).
periods.confidence: High for no nearby TC and continued shower/storm chances under ITCZ (IMN + NHC). Moderate on exact Nosara timing/amounts (IMN isolated/possible language vs light–moderate ensemble means).

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Fri–Mon)
periods.pattern: Fri (~25 Sep): GEFS mean 06Z f072 keeps SW 850 over Nicoya with a ~1006 hPa EPAC L SW of Mexico/Guatemala; EPS mean 00Z f072 has a deeper ~996 hPa EPAC L and clear SW onshore flow on the epac panel; AIFS-ENS 00Z f072 similar (~997 hPa L, W–SW 850). GFS deterministic 06Z f072 deepens a ~961 hPa EPAC low south of Mexico — treat as a TC-type feature (Polo environment), not a Costa Rica gyre. 24-h means diverge: GEFS Nicoya still light ~0.1–0.4 in; EPS wetter ~0.5–1.25 in with heavier offshore Pacific; AIFS-ENS into the weekend more moist (~0.3–1.0 in at f120). By ~Sun 27, GEFS mean f120 turns more E–NE trades over Nicoya with a Yucatán/Caribbean high (~1019 hPa), while EPS/AIFS-ENS still show SW Pacific fetch — real model split. NHC OFFPZ8 synopsis: moderate-or-weaker winds except moderate–fresh offshore El Salvador/Guatemala Thu into early Sat as a low may form just west of that area (softer than yesterday’s early-Fri CR–Guatemala wording). Not locked as a multi-day temporal or closed Central American gyre.
periods.implications: Keep late-day plans flexible Fri–Sat if SW moisture holds; treat wetter EPS/AIFS frames as a moisture signal, not a guaranteed temporales. Marine: Papagayo stays mostly light (SW/S ~10 kt, seas ~3–6 ft) with the sharper wind bump more toward El Salvador/Guatemala waters (NHC).
periods.confidence: Moderate for continued shower chances and a midweek SW-moisture signal; low–moderate for sustained temporales or a closed Central American gyre (GEFS trade return and softer NHC marine undercut yesterday’s peak concern).

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: IMN sub-seasonal (21 Sep–18 Oct) still keeps Pacífico Norte below normal (weekly Pac Norte roughly 5–90 mm for 21–27 Sep and again 28 Sep–4 Oct) with stronger-than-usual trades limiting Pacific-side rain. CPC GTH text still the 15 Sep update (valid 23 Sep–6 Oct): below-average Caribbean rainfall weeks 2–3; EPAC genesis risk coastal Mexico / open EPAC, not CR. GEFS mean f168 (~29 Sep) shows light E–NE 850 over Nicoya and light–moderate precip (~0.5–1.5 in / 24 h in places) without a local extreme bullseye or closed land gyre. Single deterministic frames can still show a wetter day — treat as scenario only.
periods.implications: No official signal for a prolonged flood-season spike on the Nicoya Pacific side; short heavy cells remain possible.
periods.confidence: Moderate for below-normal / no major local TC theme; low for day-by-day rain.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Roughly mid–late week (~Thu–Sat 24–27 Sep) if flanking EPAC lows and sustained Pacific SW low-level flow persist; GEFS mean already leans away from that by ~Sun
gyreWatch.supporting: GEFS mean 06Z f024–f072 shows SW 850 over Nicoya with EPAC Ls ~999–1006 hPa; EPS mean 00Z f072–f120 and AIFS-ENS 00Z f072–f120 keep SW onshore fetch and deep EPAC lows (~994–997 hPa); EPS epac f072 shows broad cyclonic Pacific–Central America trough structure. NHC OFFPZ8 still allows a low Thu–early Sat just west of El Salvador/Guatemala waters. Short-term IMN ITCZ / Pacific coastal rain language supports a moist Pacific start to the week.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Ensemble means do not show a closed gyre centered over Central America — pattern is flanking EPAC lows / monsoon trough plus SW moisture. GFS det deep EPAC low (~961 hPa) is a TC-type feature near Mexico (Polo), not a CR gyre. GEFS mean f120–f168 flips Nicoya toward E–NE trades. Ensemble-mean Nicoya precip stays mostly light–moderate with EPS wetter than GEFS midweek. NHC has no disturbance near Costa Rica (Hurricane Polo and TS Odalys well west/NW; Tehuantepec genesis is Mexico-parallel, 60% in 7 days). IMN sub-seasonal still favors Pacific rainfall deficit. NHC marine language is softer than yesterday on a CR–Guatemala monsoon low. Ensemble means only — no member-count probabilities.

whatChanged: Polo is now Hurricane Polo (still far from CR); Tehuantepec genesis area up to ~60% in 7 days. Biggest guidance shifts vs Mon: (1) NHC OFFPZ8 no longer highlights an early-Fri monsoon low between Costa Rica and Guatemala — wording is a possible low just west of El Salvador/Guatemala Thu–early Sat with a milder Papagayo wind field; (2) GEFS mean now turns Nicoya back toward trades by ~Sun 27, so the multi-day SW/temporales risk looks less locked than yesterday. IMN daily for Pac Norte is milder afternoon language (possible isolated rain) vs Monday’s isolated storms. Weekly adds OT#46 this weekend with little country signal. Latest listed IMN aviso remains Mon 21 Sep ITCZ — no new Tuesday aviso on the list at collection time.
practical: Best apparent outdoor windows: mornings Tue–Thu before any convective peak, with IMN keeping Pac Norte rains more isolated/possible than a locked wet day. Worth planning around: ITCZ overnight/coastal rains and isolated afternoon cells, warm inland heat (Liberia ~34°C; Nicoya ~33°C), and Papagayo SW ~10 kt with seas ~3–5 ft early week (NHC OFFPZ8 PMZ113). Watch Fri–Sat if SW moisture and the El Salvador/Guatemala low verify wetter than GEFS. No new Tuesday IMN aviso listed yet — latest is Mon 21 Sep.
